subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: Two dice are rolled at random. Find the probability distribution of the sum of the numbers on them. Find the mean of the random variable.

recall_prompt: Say how you would build the distribution of the sum of two dice and find its mean — how many outcomes there are, how you count each sum, and what you add at the end.
insider_note: The table is worth three marks and carries its own check: the counts 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 must add to 36; keep every probability over 36, so the pattern stays visible when the mean step adds the products.

steps.label: Sample space and X
steps.margin_note: First mark. Two dice give 6 × 6 = 36 equally likely ordered pairs. Name X as the sum, and say that it runs from 2 (1 + 1) to 12 (6 + 6). Both facts are needed before any probability is written.
steps.memory_tip: 6 × 6 = 36 ordered pairs, and the sum X runs from 2 to 12. Both facts before any probability.
lines: When two dice are rolled, the sample space is
Let X = the sum of the numbers on the two dice.

recall.must_convey: That there are 36 equally likely outcomes, X is the sum, and X takes the values 2 to 12.
accept: thirty six outcomes, X is the sum of the two numbers and it goes from two to twelve
the sample space has six into six equal thirty six pairs and the sum runs from two to twelve
let X be the sum, range two to twelve, total outcomes thirty six
rendu dice ki thirty six outcomes, X ante sum, two nunchi twelve varaku
write n of S equals thirty six and X equals the sum

steps.why: Every probability in the table is a count of ordered pairs out of 36, so the size of the sample space and the range of X are the two facts everything else is built from.
common_mistakes: Taking n(S) = 12 or 21 by treating (1, 2) and (2, 1) as one outcome.
Starting X at 1 or ending it at 11.
Never saying what X stands for.

steps.label: Write the distribution
steps.margin_note: Three marks — the bulk of the question. Count the pairs for each sum: 1 way for 2, 2 for 3, … 6 for 7, then down again to 1 for 12. The counts 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 add to 36, which is the check. Write every probability over 36; do not simplify, so the pattern stays visible.
steps.memory_tip: Counts 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 — they must add to 36, which is the check. Keep every fraction over 36.
lines: Count the pairs giving each sum, out of 36.

recall.must_convey: That each probability is the number of ordered pairs with that sum over 36, giving 1/36, 2/36, …, 6/36 for X = 2 to 7 and then 5/36 down to 1/36 for X = 8 to 12.
accept: count the pairs for each sum, one for two up to six for seven and back down to one for twelve, all over thirty six
the probabilities are one by thirty six two by thirty six up to six by thirty six and then down again
the counts go one two three four five six five four three two one over thirty six
prathi sum ki enni pairs unnayo lekkinchi thirty six tho divide cheyali, seven ki six ways
write the table with the counts over thirty six and check they add to thirty six

steps.why: The sum has more ways to be 7 than to be 2, so the probabilities are not equal — the table IS the answer to the first part of the question. The rise-and-fall pattern is the check that no pair was missed.
common_mistakes: Miscounting 7 as 3 ways by ignoring order.
Simplifying 2/36 to 1/18 in the table and then losing the pattern when adding.

steps.label: Find the mean
steps.margin_note: Three marks. Mean μ = Σxᵢ·P(X = xᵢ). Factor the 1/36 out and add the eleven products 2·1, 3·2, 4·3, 5·4, 6·5, 7·6, 8·5, 9·4, 10·3, 11·2, 12·1 = 252. 252/36 = 7 — the mean of two dice is twice the mean of one (7/2).
steps.memory_tip: Factor the 1/36 out; the eleven products add to 252, so μ = 7 — twice the mean of one die.

accept: mean is sigma x P of x, take one by thirty six out, the products add to two fifty two, so mu is seven
multiply each sum by its probability and add to get two fifty two by thirty six equals seven
mu equals two hundred fifty two over thirty six which is seven
prathi sum ni daani probability tho multiply chesi add cheste two fifty two by thirty six, mean seven
the mean of the sum is seven, twice the mean of one die

steps.why: The mean of a sum is the sum of the means: 7/2 + 7/2 = 7. Computing it from the table proves that, and 7 is also the check on the table — a miscounted pair moves 252 away from 7 × 36.
common_mistakes: Adding the eleven probabilities instead of the products xᵢ·P.
Writing 252/36 = 6 or 8 by an arithmetic slip in the sum of products.
Reporting 7/2, the mean of one die.
